summary: Our project is about NASA's Sojourner rover, the first successful rover on Mars. It was sent to Mars in 1997 as part of the Mars Pathfinder mission. Sojourner was a small robot that explored the surface of Mars, took pictures, and studied rocks and soil. Its mission was planned to last 7 days, but it continued working for 83 days. Even though it eventually stopped communicating with Earth, the information it collected helped scientists understand Mars better. It also helped NASA develop newer rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance. Our goal is to show that old space missions are still important and should not be forgotten. Even if a mission ends, its achievements live on.
details:
Our project is about Sojourner, the first successful rover on Mars. It was sent to Mars in 1997 as part of NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission.

Sojourner was a small robot that explored the surface of Mars. It took pictures and studied rocks and soil. Its mission was planned to last only 7 days, but it worked for 83 days.

Our project explains why Sojourner is still important today. The information it collected helped scientists understand Mars and supported the development of newer rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance.

We used NASA's website and other reliable sources to research Sojourner. We prepared our presentation using PowerPoint and Google Slides. We did not use special hardware or programming languages because our project focuses on research and storytelling.

We chose this topic because we believe old space missions should not be forgotten. Even a small rover can make a big difference in science.

Our main message is: Even if a mission ends, its achievements are never forgotten.
